newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rail workers block Le Havre line, Nantes.
newsitem.headline: French rail workers block Le Havre line, Nantes.

text.p: Striking rail workers temporarily blocked the main railway line from Paris to the port of Le Havre in northwestern France on Wednesday in a protest over government plans to create a separate railtrack company.

Separately, workers in Nantes, western France, seized a key shunting station and blocked all rail traffic in and out of the city including high-speed TGV passnger trains, in a protest over working conditions and a restructuring plan.
They said they planned to occupy the station for the remainder of the afternoon.

The SNCF state railway company said strikers from three trade unions had blocked the Paris-Rouen-Le Havre line from Tuesday night until mid-morning on Wednesday after calling a 24-hour local stoppage at the depot of Sotteville-les-Rouen, starting point of last year's 24-day national rail strike.
The SNCF diverting trains to Le Havre during the stoppage, causing delays of up to 90 minutes but few cancellations.
The local rail actions came on the 10th day of a strike by truck drivers which has increasingly choked roads in the French provinces and caused petrol shortages in several regions.

The disputes are not strictly related, but two major trade unions, the Communist-led CGT and the non-partisan Force Ouvriere, have called on members to support the truckers' action to maximise pressure on the government and employers.
Pilots at state-owned Air France and Air France Europe began a two-day strike on Wednesday over their own working conditions, which the airlines said forced them to reduce services.

Air France was running two in three of its long-haul flights but only one-quarter of its European services. Air France Europe, its mainly domestic subsidiary, said it was flying less than half of its normal schedule.
